{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java",
      "line": 73,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Constructor validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId",
      "body": "AccessTokenContext's constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, \"Null rawTokenId not allowed\") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and can later be concatenated into the encoded token ID, producing IDs ending with \":null\" or causing failures downstream. The validation message is also misleading."
    },
    {
      "file": "testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java",
      "line": 483,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Token ID event matcher uses wrong offset and inverted check",
      "body": "AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId is intended to verify the 2-character grant shortcut in positions 4-5 of the 6-character token-ID prefix, but it uses items[0].substring(3, 5) and returns false when that value equals expectedGrantShortcut. The offset is wrong and the condition is inverted, so the event assertions do not actually validate the grant encoded in token IDs. This can hide incorrect encoding in tests, and malformed short prefixes can also cause StringIndexOutOfBoundsException."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java",
      "line": 33,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "New mandatory getShortcut() breaks existing grant factories",
      "body": "Adding String getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without a default method makes all existing implementations of this factory interface fail to compile. If custom or extension grant factories are supported, this is a breaking SPI change; a default method or compatibility path is needed."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java",
      "line": 102,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Public Context copy constructor removed",
      "body": "The PR removes the public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) while adding the grantType field. Any custom grant implementation or extension that created a copy of a Context will no longer compile. This is an API contract break separate from the added grantType behavior."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java",
      "line": 106,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "setFormParams does not refresh grantType",
      "body": "OAuth2GrantType.Context.grantType is derived from formParams in the constructor, but setFormParams only replaces formParams and does not recalculate grantType. If form parameters are changed after construction, getGrantType() returns a stale value, which can then be encoded into token IDs or events."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java",
      "line": 54,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Lightweight-token decision uses global session client instead of client session",
      "body": "DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext determines whether the token is lightweight via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), which reads session.getContext().getClient(). The client session context already provides the client; using the global session context can pick the wrong client or throw NullPointerException if the session context client is not set, causing the wrong token-type shortcut to be encoded or token issuance to fail."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java",
      "line": 74,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Grant shortcuts are not validated for format",
      "body": "DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit reads gtf.getShortcut() and stores it in maps without validating that it is non-null, exactly two characters, and safe for the fixed-width token ID format. A custom grant factory returning null or a longer/shorter shortcut can cause a startup NullPointerException or produce token IDs that cannot be parsed by getTokenContextFromTokenId."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java",
      "line": 113,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Lazy shortcut registration can overwrite existing grant mappings",
      "body": "getShortcutByGrantType lazily registers a shortcut for a newly discovered grant by putting it into grantsByShortcuts without checking whether that shortcut already maps to another grant. A dynamically deployed or custom grant with a duplicate shortcut can silently overwrite an existing mapping, so token IDs later decode to the wrong grant type. The same lack of uniqueness validation exists in getGrantTypeByShortcut."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java",
      "line": 30,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "doc_defect",
      "title": "Javadoc says 3-letter shortcut but encoder requires 2 characters",
      "body": "The Javadoc for getShortcut says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', but the encoder/decoder in this PR assumes every grant shortcut is exactly two characters, because the total encoded context is fixed at six characters. The documentation should state the actual required format."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Constructor validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
findings.body: AccessTokenContext's constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and can later be concatenated into the encoded token ID, producing IDs ending with ":null" or causing failures downstream. The validation message is also misleading.

findings.title: Token ID event matcher uses wrong offset and inverted check
findings.body: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId is intended to verify the 2-character grant shortcut in positions 4-5 of the 6-character token-ID prefix, but it uses items[0].substring(3, 5) and returns false when that value equals expectedGrantShortcut. The offset is wrong and the condition is inverted, so the event assertions do not actually validate the grant encoded in token IDs. This can hide incorrect encoding in tests, and malformed short prefixes can also cause StringIndexOutOfBoundsException.

findings.title: New mandatory getShortcut() breaks existing grant factories
findings.body: Adding String getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without a default method makes all existing implementations of this factory interface fail to compile. If custom or extension grant factories are supported, this is a breaking SPI change; a default method or compatibility path is needed.

findings.title: Public Context copy constructor removed
findings.body: The PR removes the public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) while adding the grantType field. Any custom grant implementation or extension that created a copy of a Context will no longer compile. This is an API contract break separate from the added grantType behavior.

findings.title: setFormParams does not refresh grantType
findings.body: OAuth2GrantType.Context.grantType is derived from formParams in the constructor, but setFormParams only replaces formParams and does not recalculate grantType. If form parameters are changed after construction, getGrantType() returns a stale value, which can then be encoded into token IDs or events.

findings.title: Lightweight-token decision uses global session client instead of client session
findings.body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext determines whether the token is lightweight via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), which reads session.getContext().getClient(). The client session context already provides the client; using the global session context can pick the wrong client or throw NullPointerException if the session context client is not set, causing the wrong token-type shortcut to be encoded or token issuance to fail.

findings.title: Grant shortcuts are not validated for format
findings.body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit reads gtf.getShortcut() and stores it in maps without validating that it is non-null, exactly two characters, and safe for the fixed-width token ID format. A custom grant factory returning null or a longer/shorter shortcut can cause a startup NullPointerException or produce token IDs that cannot be parsed by getTokenContextFromTokenId.

findings.title: Lazy shortcut registration can overwrite existing grant mappings
findings.body: getShortcutByGrantType lazily registers a shortcut for a newly discovered grant by putting it into grantsByShortcuts without checking whether that shortcut already maps to another grant. A dynamically deployed or custom grant with a duplicate shortcut can silently overwrite an existing mapping, so token IDs later decode to the wrong grant type. The same lack of uniqueness validation exists in getGrantTypeByShortcut.

findings.title: Javadoc says 3-letter shortcut but encoder requires 2 characters
findings.body: The Javadoc for getShortcut says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', but the encoder/decoder in this PR assumes every grant shortcut is exactly two characters, because the total encoded context is fixed at six characters. The documentation should state the actual required format.
